chunks: Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Ahmad al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Urwah ibn Marwan al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Rabi' ibn Badr narrated to us, from Aban, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever preserves from me among my nation forty traditions regarding his religious affairs, seeking thereby the Face of God, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Hereafter, God will raise him on the Day of Resurrection as a learned jurist.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for memorizing and preserving forty hadiths in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a foundational incentive for the dissemination of religious knowledge, emphasizing that the preservation of forty ahadith serves as a means to attain the status of a faqih and 'alim. This tradition underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the quantity and quality of hadith transmission, linking sincere effort in learning with divine elevation on the Day of Judgment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-17 Abul Hassan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus narrated that Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Haravy quoted Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawar, on the authority of Isa ibn Ahmad al-Asqalani, on the authority of Urwah ibn Marvan al-Barqy, on the authority of Ribah ibn Badr, on the authority of Aban, on the authority of Anas that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“On the Resurrection Day, the Honorable the Exalted God shall raise anyone in my nation who remembers forty traditions regarding his religious affairs for the sake of God and the Hereafter as a learned scholar.”
